items.title: Support database connection pooling for postgresql
items.body:
So this needs tests and release notes. But I figured there might be one or two people out there who want to try this as is.

To get the pool running either set `pool` to True in the database `OPTIONS` dict or set it to a dict which then gets passed on to https://www.psycopg.org/psycopg3/docs/api/pool.html#psycopg_pool.ConnectionPool

Please note that this pool is most likely only really useful in the async case. Using a pool with a multi-process deployment (like standard gunicorn workers) is kinda useless since the will be just one concurrent request per process. Realistically speaking, this only becomes interesting in the sync case once we can have multithreaded gil-free python :D

items.title: Fixed #33012 -- Added Redis cache backend.
items.body:
ticket-33012

This PR is in accordance with this [GSoC project](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/projects/#6292871491092480)
The detailed proposal can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_gIa_17uCNlwJTmqiMLkiVtRgTOD2MvHpy4NNFvKBWc/edit?usp=sharing)

This PR aims at adding support for Redis to be used as a caching backend with Django. As redis is the most popular caching backend, adding it to django.core.cache module would be a great addition for developers who previously had to rely on the use of third party packages.

Major Tasks : 
- [x] Create RedisCache as a subclass of the BaseCache class and implement methods
- [x] Create PickleSerializer to serialize data before storing it into redis
- [x] Extend existing tests for new class
- [x] Add Documentation and Release Notes
- [x] Add additional tests for RedisCache and RedisCacheClient
- [x] Moving `PickleSerializer` from `django.contrib.sessions.serializers` to `django.core.serializers.base`. See [comment](https://github.com/django/django/pull/14437/#discussion_r699197718) #14827

Remaining Tasks :
- [x] Waiting for #14802
- [ ] Documenting extra arguments. See [comment](https://github.com/django/django/pull/14437/#discussion_r699194492)

Future Tasks : 
- [ ] Add support for providing `username` and `password` in `OPTIONS`. This will be possible in the upcoming version of redis-py
- [ ] Milli second support (To be discussed)

Let me expand on my previous comment to explain why I think that the latest refactor is wrong:

* With default connections and non-persistent connections we close a connection every request and reopen it every request. As such we need one query to set the timezone every request
* With persistent connections the connection stays open and the timezone is only set once per connection. The assumption is that the view doesn't change the timezone in a bad way.
* With a pool we are basically back to the first case, as far as Django is concerned we are closing the connection every request (but in reality put it back to the pool) and once we check it out again it should not net to apply a new timezone (ie it behaves like a persistent connection)

To test the behavior I would recommend the following (manually in a project, forget the tests for now): 

 * Disable pooling, set a timezone in the settings that is != your default timezone and enable query logging in postgres. Verify that the timezone is set every request.
 * Now enable persistent connections and verify that the timezone is only set once per connection
 * Now disable persistent connections and enable a pool with a maxsize of 1, verify that the timezone is set once per connection
